description: PaperMind 团队原创的合成评测语料，不代表真实医学研究结论。

papers.title: Alpha-MIL: Gated Multiple-Instance Learning for Synthetic Stage Prediction

chunks.content: Alpha-MIL encodes every tile with a pretrained ResNet-34 feature extractor. The encoder produces a 512-dimensional vector for each tile before pooling.
The Alpha-MIL aggregator applies gated attention and retains the top 32 instances. A compact consistency penalty encourages neighboring synthetic regions to receive similar scores.
The Orion cohort contains 240 synthetic whole-slide records split 60 percent for training, 20 percent for validation, and 20 percent for testing. Alpha-MIL obtains 0.860 accuracy and 0.910 AUC.
Most Alpha-MIL errors occur between adjacent synthetic stages. Future work will evaluate external centers and replace the handcrafted encoder with a foundation-model representation.

papers.title: Beta-Transformer: Sparse Attention for Synthetic Slide Analysis

chunks.content: Beta-Transformer uses a Swin-T encoder to create 1024-dimensional patch embeddings. Positional coordinates are added before sparse self-attention.
The sparse attention block selects 64 landmarks and uses two transformer layers. This design reduces quadratic interaction cost while preserving long-range synthetic context.
The Nova benchmark provides 300 synthetic slides. Beta-Transformer reaches 0.840 accuracy and 0.890 AUC, using AdamW with a learning rate of 3e-4.
Beta-Transformer is strongest on broad contextual patterns but less stable on tiny regions. The authors propose multi-scale landmarks as the next synthetic experiment.

papers.title: GraphPath-MIL: Neighborhood Graphs for Synthetic Tissue Classification

chunks.content: GraphPath-MIL connects every patch to its six nearest spatial neighbors. Node attributes combine color statistics with 256-dimensional ConvNeXt-T features.
Three graph-attention layers propagate local evidence before mean pooling. GraphPath-MIL trains with Adam at a learning rate of 2e-4 and weight decay of 1e-5.
The Atlas set contains 180 synthetic slides and uses five-fold cross-validation. GraphPath-MIL reports 0.820 accuracy, 0.800 macro F1, and 0.870 AUC.
GraphPath-MIL improves local interpretability through explicit edges. Its main limitation is graph construction time, so future work will test adaptive neighborhood sampling.
